rules.basis: BUY: a stream takes a replica count with a default, but one stream has one leader and JetStream does not split a stream, so growing writers needs fero to cut subjects over more streams, which it did not build (E-44)

CELL (referee): the cell count is fixed at define, 16 by default (P fixN); 16 cells give 7 to 15 writers' worth under skew (E-18 B4), below F_w = 64, and the only growth is a re-key whose count 'is chosen per re-key' (E-17). Nothing in the row chooses it: P has no '+ rule' and C is self (healing only, no planner). If F_w is lowered to 7 or less, the default 16 is enough: met

ISR: partitions are fixed when a resource is defined (P fixN) and never move, split or re-key, and SPACE gives no default count; if the default gives fewer writers than F_w, a count must be chosen up front, as in Kafka

No count exists to choose: the 4,096 slots are fixed by fero (A-16), copies defaults to 3, full replicas default to every server up to 5, and groups grow and shrink by slot moves under one policy (A-18; E-18 simulated it to 64 groups). E-22's 22 examples set no count
LANE: the 64 lanes per project are fixed by fero and copies is one project default; its writer ceiling is SC-03's matter, not a number the user picks
SPLIT and PD: groups (regions) split, and in PD merge, by size and load by themselves (decision 20a; TiKV's shape, cited), and the replica count has a default

rules.basis: BUY: tenancy is theirs (N theirs). One NATS cluster per project keeps projects apart at 2.4 to 3.7 times the cost at small loads (E-41); a shared cluster would lean on NATS accounts, which fero does not control. Not tested

The hosted shape pools projects on one log tier (N tier; for OBJ the object store itself) or one process (N pool, with isolation by V8 isolates never tested, G-25): on a shared journal a tenant at its quota raised another's p99 1.40 to 1.59 times against 1.1 (E-35), so it takes a byte budget per tenant (A-29), which was not built, and keys per project are not designed. If J is not changed, the shared tier is not allowed and the row fails as it stands
By construction nothing holds more than one project: one cluster and one set of processes and disks per project (N proc), with no log tier and no object store among its options (S lsm, S walg)

No log tier and no pooled process (N proc): one process and one volume per project, as J promises (E-35 reasons it keeps tenants off one disk; not tested). But the hosted object store (S +tier) holds many projects, and keys per project at rest and the lack of any read path across projects are not designed in any row

else.basis: not judged: no judged row holds this mix of tags on the deciding axes

parts.why: N and S decide where projects share bytes: a pooled tier or process (N tier, pool) is open on the restated J and fails if J stays; a project's own processes with an object-store tier (N proc, S +tier) are open on the store; with neither (N proc, S lsm or walg) nothing is shared, met. BUY is theirs (R outside).
